title: Blind Boone, Charleston music teachers and church music
summary: White names Blind Boone and the Charleston teachers who trained him, and describes the city's churches, organs and choirs.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I'm just trying to think about another great, yeah, Scott Joplin. Oh, yes.

What are you going to do about Blind Boone and Scott Joplin? What are you going to do about it? Now, Blind Boone did not read any music, but he had a teacher when he was a little boy. He did have his sight and he read Blind before he- He came from Missouri somewhere.
That's right. My mother always talked about him when she was a girl.

And Blind Boone played the piano so skillfully. All the compositions just as perfect. You take the school out here and look at it if you feel like it. Because he came on a concert tour to Charleston. And Professor Dart and Professor Ankrum and Professor Ranson and Professor Sawyer and Professor Smalls and Professor J. Donovan Moe, who was still alive in his 90s. Right in the same class now with Dr. Dubois. The two old men look alike. Those men were music instructors and they laid special stress on how well you played the accompaniment. Because we used to give cantatas and these dramatized versions of this thing and that thing, Martha, all of these old major compositions. I can't think of a- I can't think of a- This liturgical work on the- Vows of- The Bohemian girl-

We used to give all these things in churches in Charleston. Charleston was a city noted for its finer churches. They had a corner meeting house like they have today. You see Charleston had about 11 churches in it. All cathedral styles. Plush floors. Fine seats. Centenary church. Emanuel. Big Emanuel and Little Emanuel. But they were both magnitudes and size. A house. Thousands and more people. Balkans all around. Pipe organ. The biggest pipe she ever laid out on. And they chimed. And you can hear the chimes in Charleston until today. And the Negro churches had pipe organs just equal to any of them. You could go to any of them. Those are fine churches. Now all these men. They sat as conductors or organists in these trials. And the services were just fine. They didn't have this raucous type of service. These things like Church of God Christ and stomping all around here. They came on the scene here in the last 25 years. You see. And all these men I mentioned to you had- They were choir masters. Organists and conductors with choir in these various churches. See. Asked Edmund. And Edmund was an old man in New York. Asked him about his father. I'm going to ask you a bit more about Scott Joplin if you knew him.
